question: Question linked to the image nº24 Brain CT scan performed as a matter of urgency in the case of cranioencephalic traumatism. What is your diagnosis?:
analysis: In cases of cranioencephalic trauma, the presence of a hyperdense area on a CT scan typically indicates a hematoma. An acute subdural hematoma is often crescent-shaped and can cross suture lines, while an epidural hematoma is usually lens-shaped and does not cross suture lines. Cortical injury would show areas of contusion, and intraventricular hemorrhage would present with blood in the ventricles. Without the image, the most common urgent finding in trauma is an acute subdural hematoma, especially if the patient has altered consciousness or neurological deficits.
